utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mansfield. To I could remind you, sir, of the affirmation that you made at the beginning of your evidence is still applicable.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wonder if the Albanian version of the interview that we started to go through yesterday is still available. I believe it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, Witness, just so you may get your bearings, we were beginning to go through an interview which you signed that took place on the 13th of July, 2003 at the regional crime squad offices in relation to your arrest in relation to the illegal possession of drugs and weapons. And we -- if you just kindly look at it again. Eventually you managed to find the first question and answer and I want now to come to the next question and answer after that. So if you would kindly look on the first page of your Albanian version, the second question is a question that reads in English, and if you just follow the Albanian. The question is English is: "Q. This wrapping by paper, this Kinder egg and this amount of powder, what do you think this is?" Now, do you see that question in your Albanian version?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to deal with the answer that you gave. The answer that is recorded and you signed is: "A. I think you are wrong. This is not drug. And I'm sure about this. If you want, I can eat it all." Do you see that answer?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, the question I have is: If as you now tell the Tribunal that some of the material that was in your house was, you thought, fertiliser brought from abroad, why did you not tell the place at any stage in this interview that was found in your house was fertiliser? Why didn't you say that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said this and if this is the statement then it should contain what I told them. It must have been written somewhere. Regarding this Kinder egg, this I didn't see. I already said even earlier. They told me that they had found it, but I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: We'll move on because you'll see as we go through there is no reference to fertiliser at any stage. So we'll just move on to the third question. This is an important question by the police officer: "Q. We have information that you and your wife are drug users. You and your wife sell drugs in Pristina. What can you tell us about this?" Do you see that question?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now listen, please, to the answer carefully on this one. You indicate that your wife doesn't use it. And you haven't been out in Pristina for two and a half months. I want you to look at this next bit, the next sentence. It says: "I am a drug user (heroin) and I stopped using drugs for about ten days." Do you see that answer?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's not written here. This is missing, this sentence that you are putting to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. I appreciate what you're saying. In the Albanian copy that has been sent, the -- some of the copies have not come out. But the original indicated what I have just said in English, so would you just listen for a moment to what the original Albanian said. I'll read the answer again, the sentence I want to ask you about. What it originally said in Albanian was this: "I am an a drug user (heroin) and I stopped using drugs for about ten days." And not all of that has come out on your copy. Do you remember telling the police that you were a drug user, using the words, "I am a drug user (heroin) and I stopped using drugs for about ten days." Do you remember telling them that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I don't remember this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You see, --

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And this question that you mentioned about my wife, this too I don't seem to remember. That they asked me about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: See, the point I want to make is a simple one. You never tell the police in July that in fact you stopped using and being addicted to drugs in January, maybe February at the latest and that you have been off drugs for several months. You never say that, do you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I said that. I don't know. I believe I said the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. We're going to go through this and you will see that in fact at no stage do you ever tell the police in this interview that you have had treatment; that you have been off drugs for months, and that your last addiction was at the end of 2002; and you may have used a couple of times in January/February. You never tell them that and I want to ask you: Why is it that you don't?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you that I already told them. But I don't know what they have written down. I have already told the police that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: We're just going through it and you'll see it's not here. Now can I just move to the next question. Would you please identify it. It's the fourth question. "Q. Did you ever sell any narcotics to somebody else?" Do you see that question?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And your answer is: "No." Isn't it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And that wasn't the truth either, was it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are police suspicions. When somebody is under arrest of course there are suspicions against that person. But that is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry. Please understand. You told the police that you'd never sold any narcotics to anyone else and that was a lie, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not a lie.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: The truth is, even on your own account, in fact you had been involved in narcotics being sold to someone else. On your account, it's as a middleman; correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So sorry. So why didn't you tell them that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already told them. I told them that I was playing the role of an intermediary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, Witness, every time you say you told them, none of this -- every time you say that, none of it is in this interview at all. It is not recorded. Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interview was taken by a German and an Albanian policeman. The Albanian policeman I'm sure even now that he didn't know English well. I read the statement. I don't know why I didn't correct the mistakes. Probably I didn't pay due attention. I didn't think it was important to correct each and every one of the mistakes. Then I signed it. The signature is mine, of course. Even though you can forge a signature, of course. But this is mine. I don't deny it that it's not the original one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Next question. "Q. Police have information" -- do you see the question? Fifth one -- "that you regularly sold drugs to persons we will mention." Now I'm not going to read out all of the name in public. One of the names, the third one is the name of somebody I asked about yesterday. Do you remember the third name? I don't ask that you trade out, but it's there.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And in fact on your version yesterday, you had had dealings with drugs with him, hadn't you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now we'll look at your answer. The answer indicates that you know one of them, you don't know another. But in fact you don't mention that third name at all, do you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe they didn't ask me about him. If I was asked about him, I must have certainly said yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Witness, are you understanding any of this? The question is about him. They do ask about -- the police have information that you had regularly sold and there are the names are, spelt out: one, two, three, four, five six names. They do ask about him.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. This I know. I know him now and then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Sixth question. "Q. We didn't ask you if you know them," says the police officer, "but if you sold drugs to these persons, the names that I mentioned," and then I suggest comes another lie. You said "no." That's a lie, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't sell drugs. I didn't say then and now that I sold drugs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I see. The difference is you gave them away. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what you say, you gave them away -- their names away. What I knew I said I know. The persons I didn't know, I said I don't know them directly. Personally I know them through -- by sight. Because I never had contacts with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You told us yesterday in the case of the third name -- all right? The third name in that list. I think for these purposes it doesn't matter if I mention his name, this part of it, publicly, Ari. You told us yesterday about your dealings with drugs with that person and you lied to the police in July about that person, saying, No when you were asked about them.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way I understand the question is do you know them, and do you have -- have you ever sold drugs to them. And the answer was no, I didn't sell drugs to them. This is how I read this sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm going to move on. You were asked about your family personal incomings. You say -- just follow the question and answer -- "We have only my salary. Son used to work." And then you mention where working and so on. "The amount is small, only to survive." Next question. "Q. You just told us that you're a drug user except these last ten days. For how long are you a drug addict?" Do you see that question?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So the police officer was making it clear that what you had told him was that you'd only, as it were, stopped using drugs for the last ten days. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And in fact when you appeared before the judge in relation to this matter, you repeated this, didn't you? You told the judge in Pristina that you had been off drugs only for the last 15 days in that case. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that. Maybe I have said this, but I don't remember that. Maybe I have said this, but I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, never mind whether you remember. It wasn't true on your account, was it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you I don't remember. To have said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'd like you to concentrate for a moment because I suggested right at the beginning of the cross-examination that you were a user and -- not only a user but a dealer, but in the context of this question a user of drugs throughout the time you had been interviewed by the OTP and so forth in May and then in June, and you were using up to the time of this arrest or near to it in July. And that is the truth, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at all. That I was a user, that's true. But that I was a dealer, that's not true. That's not true. Up to that time, I was not a user.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, let's look at your answer to that question. The answer is: "A. Since October 2001 when I was kidnapped since that time, I have tried to get away from it for two or three months, but I couldn't." Do you see that answer?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have gone off it several times and I have interrupted it for one, two or three months. But it was not possible for me to do that without taking the necessary medicaments which it was very difficult for me to come by.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And what we will see as we go through the next questions is had a you were buying heroin right up to the very recent past, just before this interview. Just follow. The next question is: "Q. How you use heroin?" "A. By nose. "Q. What is the amount you use per day?" Have you followed that question? "What is the amount that you use per day?"

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your answer: "A. Recently I have used it for 20 cents, one fifth of a gramme." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. Was that true?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Recently means, at least for me it means that the time that I have left it. It doesn't mean that it was the day when I was arrested. This is what I had in mind when I used word "recently," meaning that I have used it very little then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Just go on to the next question. The officer say this: "Q. You're sitting here for one hour and you're sniffing. Do you agree that you have used drugs more than you have told us, that you have used heroin?" Do you see that question.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You suggest of course that it's got nothing to do with drug addiction. You say: "I've got a flu and this is the reason."

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From 1.30 to 7.00 in the morning I was tied against a jeep outside. It was cold and I got a cold. And he suspected me when I was sniffing because he said this is what people who are drug addicts do. That is what the German officer told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Next question: "Q. How much money do you spend for heroin per month? And your answer to that question: "A. I don't know exactly. Around 100 Euros, up to 200 Euros per month." [Microphone not activated] answer?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not -- it doesn't show on my copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No, I appreciate some of them haven't come out. But did you -- were you spending around 100 Euros to 200 Euros a month in 2003?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 2003? No, that's not true. The question was, for during all of the time, how much I used and how much I spent in total.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No. The question was -- just follow how it's put in the Albanian. This is how we have it in English: "How much money do you spend for heroin per month?"

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes but it doesn't specify the month. I don't see that the question indicated the month or the year. In that case my answer would have been different.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, we're going to come to the month in a moment. "From whom did you get or buy heroin?" And again, this may not have come out on your copy. "From whom did you get or buy heroin?" Was the question. "A. I got it from many persons, up to 100 persons." "Q. From whom did you buy heroin? "A. I got it from Ramiz in Gjilane. Velixh [phoen] in Gjilane who is in prison, and others," and so on. Do you see that answer?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now I just want to pause for a moment and ask you whether in fact as I did yesterday, that Ramiz from Gjilane is the same one that your son told on the 10th of February was he bought heroin, ten grammes in his case. Is it the same one?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. You may ask him. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now I'm asking you. Is it the same one, because he met a Ramiz at the theatre in Gjilane. He met him also in Pristina and he was given ten grammes and they were going to go into business together. Could this be the same person?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I answered your question. I told you I don't know. But when I read the next sentence, there is another name, and it has got nothing to with the reality. This name was not mentioned in my statement. I think this -- this has been added later and this name didn't exist then. "Skender" it read -- writes here. It has got nothing to do with that day. I'm very certain about that. It is linked with some another affair, quite another affair.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Move on. The next question is: "Q. From which person did you buy heroin on the last six Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. months?" Do you see that question?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And you say: "Recently," -- again, a word that you have used before -- "I have bought from a person from Ferizaj and from a person from Gjilane and Ramiz introduced me to this person." And then you go on to give more details which I don't need to read all out. So again, you're indicating to the interviewing officer that you have in fact bought heroin recently, within the previous six months.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I am telling you again: This is not what was said on the 13th of July. This is entirely different thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So again, it's --

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it is similar. But the things are not exactly as they were then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Once again, this is a mistake you overlooked, is it, when you signed?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This statement, I told you, is not the one of the 13th of July. It's not the same. I know what I said then. The first page is similar. But many things are not mentioned in that statement. I have given three, not one, statements: 13th of July, 15th of July, 16th of July, and the 18th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm going to go to speed things up for the rest of this recorded interview as it is set out here. If you run down the page after that question. You are asked more details about Ramiz, telephone numbers, where you met him, a description of him, his age, and the fact that you knew that he dealt in drugs. And then towards the bottom of our page, could you come the question which is: "Q. How many times did you buy drugs from Ramiz approximately?" I'll read the question again. "How many times did you buy drugs from Ramiz approximately?" Do you see that question?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, look at the answer that is recorded: "A. More than ten times in amounts of about ten grammes every time I have bought from him." Is that true?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's very true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now the next question: "Q. Do you remember when you buy for the first time and for the last time?" You see that next question?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I can't. It doesn't appear on my copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Sorry, it's another occasion when the Albanian has not copied in the fax -- where it has been transmitted. But just bear with me. This is the -- can I just repeat. Because it's not come out on yours I'll repeat it. "Q. Do you remember when you did -- do you remember when you did buy for the first time and for the last time?" Your answer according to the English record is: "A. Last year," for the first time, "and a month ago I bought five grammes in the amount of 70 Euros." Now, is that true?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't see it. And I don't know I have bought it. But I thought at the beginning -- I told at the beginning that I was mediators [as interpreted] in several instances but I didn't purchase for myself during 2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Final question on this part of it: Had you bought five grammes of heroin a month before this interview in June 2003?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So assuming they have it down correctly how could you be telling the police that you had done so?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- my supposition is that a mistake may have been made. This is the first for me to see it. I don't know what statement you are talking about. I have my own suspicions about the content of the statement. Some things here are absolutely different from what I said. Even some names.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now I'm going to ask you about one more area in this -- these interviews that took place in July 2003. And in your copy, if you would look at the page, I think it's the -- yes, it's the third page of your copy. And the third page of our copy you will see a third of the way down the third page your signature appears with a line underneath it and then underneath that it says continuation and then your name is there of the statement. Do you see that page and the part I'm dealing with now?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, then just passing down that page, you will see there's a question. "Q. Can you tell us this? Yesterday you told us that a year ago" - so that's 2002 - "you have seen in Peja 113 kilogrammes of heroin. Can you tell us where you have seen this and to whom was this heroin -- who possessed it and with whom were you when you saw this amount of drug, heroin?" Now, do you see that question?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's under the signature or above the signature?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No. It's under the first signature. And it's right at the bottom of the third page, both in the English and in the Albanian. It's the last question on the third page.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes I see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, I asked you very carefully without showing you this interview yesterday whether you had seen 113 kilogrammes in Peja and you were emphatic that you not seen any heroin. You had only heard it talked about. Do you remember saying that yesterday?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Before we look at this answer, do you want to change it today?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't want to change it. It's so. I am putting it to you again: This statement was not taken on the 13th of July. Because that was shorter. This conversation has taken place in the jeep with two persons. One was British one was Albanian. This is what I am telling you. It was on the way to Peja.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... is said on this page which you've signed just beneath it in your copy. This is the answer: "A. I was with friend." I'm not going to read out all the names, somebody from Pristina, "and where he lives and a car," which I again I mentioned to you yesterday, "black in colour." You give his age. The person that possessed this heroin was that person's friend. Met the person in Pristina; you name where you met him. And this person "took us to his house." And then, again, the person I mentioned yesterday "and me are witnesses, that we saw this amount of drugs. Don't know his name, I don't remember it for the moment but this person had a house when you get out of the Peja towards Decan on the right-hand side. The basement of this house, he had his own company, he was dealing with food items, trading. He told us that he had a contract in Turkey and as he said they couldn't fulfil the obligations and they gave this person heroin to compensate for the goods and the person was then a suspect." And you give a age and he had a friend from Peja. Now, do you see that answer?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it. But this is not what you are saying. Now I remember very well the statement I in Pristina at the police station. It was in English. It was read out to me it was translate today me and I signed it. It was in English. So this statement, I'm telling you, it's not at all true. This happened on the way in the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I just want to be clear because I'm going to leave this interview now. Are you saying that this interview didn't take place and this is a forged signature on the bottom of this page?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I'm not saying this. The signature is mine. This is authentic. The statement was not a proper statement. It was a conversation in the car not in an office where you can sit and people can take notes. Words can change. Many things are not as the talk took place. You can prove this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honours I'm going to move from that. And I wonder if in fact that particular record might become itself an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I believe it's DM3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: L.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Excuse me, DL3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That will be DL3, Mr. Mansfield.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, you will recall yesterday, Witness, I indicated what I suggest was the reason why there had been a raid on your premises on the 13th of July. I'm not going through that again in public. But I want to show you a document in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, what I'd like you to do is - not aloud - I'd like to you read what is in that statement to yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honours, I understand there are English copies of this, which you may have. Yes, I'm obliged.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Could you kindly indicate when you've had enough time to read it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And in order to examine just some of it, obviously I will not do it in public. But this is a statement which indicates in general terms that you are a heroin user; that you are dangerous when you don't have the heroin; that you are also a dealer, naming customers and suppliers, names which we have already dealt with in another context; and that in fact lately, and we understand although this is not dated, it's a July statement; in other words, sometime close to the time of your arrest, even the Thursday before you were buying heroin, and that you assaulted the maker of the statement. Do you understand that that's a summary of what it is claiming?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand what you are saying but this is not true. Now you have started to deal with sick persons with intrigues, with lies, with minors. No problem, you can continue along these lines. That's not a problem for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour it might be sensible to do it in private session just for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: At this time, just turning to another member of your family, had the prison sentence which had been passed on another member of your family actually been served at all by this time in July 2003?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in prison, he was convicted. He filed an appeal to the higher-instance court but the answer did not come back. And he still hasn't received it. I don't know whether he was pardoned or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: What I want to do with you now just before we move to the October period, I want to make at that plain to you -- the suggestion that I make on behalf of Mr. Limaj is you agreed in the end to cooperate because you had a series of major problems that had you to face. And may I just put them to you so you see what the whole picture was in July 2003. Firstly, you had no regular employment at that time, did you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whenever I wanted to, I did have an employment. And I never depended on 120 Euros per month as a payment. My craft was like that that could offer me ten times more, and you can only find a few in Kosovo who depend on 120 Euros nowadays.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now would you answer the question. You had no regular employment in July 2003, did you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I was on unpaid leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Secondly, you had been evicted from the flat in Pristina and you were having to live in burnt-out premises?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true. We have four houses, one three-storey house, the others one-storey houses. My house was also built. It had all of the conditions fulfilled. It had a bathroom, toilet. And in addition we have another house which -- where nobody lives for the moment. I left the apartment after I spoke with the owner. Only some things that remained that I left behind were then taken away from the apartment by the habitat organisation and I have an application filed with Habitat organisation and I have an application with habitat.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You spoke to the owner. Is that the ex-police officer?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the owner, the female owner. His wife came to the police station in Vranjefc. We spoke in the presence of the police and we agreed what to do further.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You had also in 2003 at that time a family to support?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. You were facing a situation in which you were going to be charged and were charged with firearms offences and drugs offences, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Was never worried about this, whether I would be charged for weapons or 30 cents of heroin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You see, the police didn't believe it was just 30 cents of heroin. You were believed to be a dealer. We have just been through the interview. You realised that the police believed that you were a dealer as well as a user and in fact other members of your family. You knew that, didn't you, that that's what they believed?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true. These are based on the statement of the minor and this is not true. The judge would have thought the same like you that I was a user. The weapons were old ones out of use and this was not much of a concern for me. I would have served a small sentence and that would be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Just dealing with the question of sentence. So far as the unlicensed or illegal possession of firearms and ever drugs are concerned, you have a previous conviction in relation to weapons, and therefore, I suggest, you were facing a prison sentence of far longer than six to nine months, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was convicted about weapons, never for drugs. I was convicted in 1995, sentenced to three months' imprisonment. The second-instance court diminished it, made it two months. This was in 1995 when Milosevic was still in power. After the war I was never arrested and I was not convicted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And the position was -- which I just move on into the October, November period, and I don't intend at all for you to indicate the details of this other than you were provided with a completely new opportunity, were you not? In other words, you and your family were relocated, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, my family is a big family. Even in the 1980s, beginning of 1990s I knew the entire Europe and I could have gone somewhere to seek for asylum. Even today, thanks for that help, but it is true that I will return soon because of the situation that became very dangerous, I Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. accepted that in order not to put my family at risk. But now I have second thoughts, and this is not true what you are saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No. You accepted relocation for -- does it involve all of your family?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And in addition to relocation, have you been provided with accommodation?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shelter. A temporary shelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. Is the answer yes?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it wasn't an apartment but a temporary shelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And have you been assisted with employment?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I live from Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Have you been provided with any financial support?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. Only the money that I got for food. And I still receive it from Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And in relation to this, were you ever told that in fact whatever you may have said in your statements and so on to the OTP, the Office of the Prosecutor, about your knowledge of what went on during the war, that you yourself would not be prosecuted?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not ask to be released from prison. When I was released from prison, it was in the statement, but nobody told me that if I had committed something during the war that I would not be held responsible. Even if I have committed something, I will be held responsible for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You see, the reason I ask you is, that in your case -- may I just explain? On occasions a witness is warned that they don't have to answer questions in case the answers might incriminate them. Now you weren't given that warning. So is it your understanding, therefore, you could be prosecuted even now?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not if I give a statement and not if I don't give a statement. And my statement does not link with what you are saying. There is another reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: The question is relatively simple: Do you understand at the moment that you might be prosecuted for actions that you took on your account during the war in relation to Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand that. I understand that I could be prosecuted for things that I have committed at any time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And on your version, of course I'm not going through the detail of everything; we've heard it. On your account, of course, you have done things that you shouldn't have done. We mentioned some of them yesterday, didn't we?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the things that I shouldn't have done. Which things are these?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You've really forgotten since yesterday some of the incidents of violence by you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday I said that it wasn't desirable but for that time, it was quite normal to lift someone's head with the barrel of a gun. You could not just go to someone and hug him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm going to move to -- if you wouldn't mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I think there was a bundle, Your Honour, of documents that the Prosecutor put before you; it's tab 11. I would like the witness, please, to have this because it has an Albanian translation. It relates to the October stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, while that is being done I just noted that Exhibit DL3 needs to be put under seal. I don't know if it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It wasn't. I think you're right. It will be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you. I noticed it also but I was going to wait. The exhibit number is P166 and it is under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honours, in this bundle, it's tab 11, and it's the order that was made on October the 16th, 2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And, Witness, you have it in Albanian with that date on. You will see on the first page of the Albanian in the middle of the page your name appears and then there's an order that you be declared a cooperative reasons. Do you see that page in the Albanian?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see it. I see where the name is mentioned the way you just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. Just to give you the context of this document what is the judge is ordering and you will see on that page the two offences relating to weapons and drugs, including acts facilitating sale. That's the charges in which -- in relation it which your cooperation is sought. And then on the next page -- it will be paragraph 4. There is set out there points, certainly major points, that the judge is suggesting should be the basis of cooperation. "Such cooperation will include and but is not limited to." You see that in the introductory paragraph in 4. So look for number 4 and then the sentence that is just before the subparagraph (a) where your name appears again. Are you following?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask you now, in particular, matters that relate to the person I represent, Fatmir Limaj. Paragraph (a) states both your name testifying that you saw Limaj there Lapusnik several times. Now I'm going to take this in stages. Let's take that point first, shall we. I'm going to ask do you?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Excuse me, I'm sorry to interrupt. I think just for the record to be clear it should be stated that in the preamble paragraph 4 there, it states that these are matter that are derived from the witness' prior interviews with the OTP. In other words, these aren't matters that are being told to the witness that he should testify about, but these are summarised from his prior interviews with the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, I accept that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Witness, you do understand that this is a summary of what you have already told the judge. Do you follow, Witness?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now I am going to ask but some of these points now. And this point comes first: How many times do you say to this Tribunal that you saw Fatmir Limaj in Lapusnik? And that's the whole area, obviously.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. And then you were pressed by Mr. Whiting, the Prosecutor, a few days ago about what you meant. And I'm going to press you. What do you mean by "several"?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, several times cannot specify whether it was two, five or seven times. When I gave it a second thought, those that came to my mind, those meetings, those I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There is a need for redaction of a use of the name of the witness some minutes ago. That will be attended to. We're not in a position to overcome the fact that it has already reached the public gallery. I think nothing more can be done about that at the moment, Mr. Mansfield, so if we can carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. I apologise if it was me. I don't think I mentioned it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's not on the record; it's been already taken out of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: But it was in the oral --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, since -- you do appreciate that is a very important matter for the Tribunal itself to discover in relation to Lapusnik -- one of the matters -- how often Fatmir Limaj was there. And if you're telling the truth and have a memory, I would like to know or the Tribunal would like to know what your answer is to this. Is it two times, is it seven times or is it ten or is it so often that you really can't remember, or don't you know?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know it very well. Approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Approximately how many then?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that in the beginning, I said several times without designating the right number. Later on I gave it a thought. Not even today -- I don't know today that how many times it was. It can be even more than ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. Ten is what you told Mr. Whiting and the Tribunal. When you were asked about in relation to a statement you made, you said -- very recently you said 15 or 16 times. But when you were asked originally about this matter in May 2003, you gave a completely different version, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. As I said, for the moment, I didn't think of the exact number. But if I give it a thought I might know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: In May - so that it's clear, it's May 2003 interview - if there are pages, it's page 22. I'm not asking you to have it for the moment. You were asked in May 2003 what was Fatmir Limaj's position and you said: "He's come to Lapusnik two or three times all in all." Didn't you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The official times that he came for a reason, for the soldiers, even today, I will say that it couldn't be more than two, three or four times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now I want you to be careful and make no -- Now, Witness, I want you to be careful. I do not wish for you to speculate, to guess, to make assumptions. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I follow you very well, and I don't like to make suggestions or assumptions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Therefore, on that basis would it be fair to say that you only saw Fatmir Limaj in Lapusnik on two or four occasions?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I saw him more times but as I said, when he came officially for all of the soldiers there, these times were two, three or four times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm sorry, this won't do, you see. When you were pressed about this in May it wasn't about official times. You were pressed and Mr. Whiting who has been asking you questions said: "And you saw him two or three times in Lapusnik." And you said in relation to that question about seeing him: "Well, few times probably three or four times." That's had a you told Mr. Whiting in May 2003, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct. This is how I said it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And that's the truth. You only saw him three or four times, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that when I gave it a second thought, and considering the official visits as well, I know that I have seen him more times. But this is what I said on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And just so that it's clear on this topic: You never saw him in the compound which you have called the prison, did you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's true that I have never seen him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And you never saw him entering the compound either, did you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is very much true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And you never saw him in the road outside either, did you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the road, I have seen the vehicles, not him. It is true that I haven't seen him there. But he could have come to the kitchen or to the staff. That doesn't mean that he went to the prison, if the vehicle was there. There is not what I have said and it is not what I'm saying now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want to -- if you wouldn't mind going back to the document that you have in front of you with paragraph 4(a) where you will see -- again I make it clear, and in fairness to you this is a summary of what has been said to the judge. A specific occasion is mentioned here. Approximately the 15th of May, 1998 when Limaj said he was the general commander of the zone and that Isak Musliu would be in charge of Lapusnik instead of Ymer Alushani and that soldiers should report to Musliu who would then report to him, Limaj. I want to ask you just before the break about that. Now are you understanding what I want to ask you about?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know what you're going to ask, but I understand what you have just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, what I'm going to suggest to you is: that there was no such occasion when he came to Lapusnik and indicated he was the general commander of the zone, and that Isak would be in charge of Lapusnik. That just never happened. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm following you very well. But it is not the way you are saying it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now for these purposes and I am sorry to give you an another document to put alongside. Could you have P165 in front of you please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document is under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, we have heard from you already on a number of occasions that this diary, as it's entitled, was compiled from notes made on other sheets of paper at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Excuse me, sorry. We have the original here that probably would be better to use.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. May he have the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now you have the original. I want to ask you this first of all: You mentioned this diary to the investigators at a very early stage in May 2003 when you were first questioned. You mentioned it on -- twice in those early interviews. And you thought -- that the way you put it was that your belongings had been thrown out of the flat or the apartment in Pristina along with the diary but you thought you still had it. Do you remember telling them that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, but I said that I have a notebook with some notes which is not completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well what you actually said, save you looking it up: "I have to look through my things as I've been evicted and everything has been thrown. But I'm a hundred per cent sure that I possess, have it." And that's the diary. "My things were thrown out the other day, were thrown out in the yard. I think I can find it." Just pausing. Were your things thrown out of the apartment?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I didn't make it such a drastic thing as to mention that they were thrown in the yard. Things that remained were taken outside, a cupboard, some carpets, a washing machine. And some books, some notes. These things were taken outside. I thought that they were lost and that's why I wasn't sure I had it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: The question I have is: When was it that you were able to find the diary and show it in fact to the investigators?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that as soon as I mentioned it, I gave them the diary the next day or a day after that. This is what I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: All right. Now, the object of the diary was in fact - is this right - to record important events during the war, that is, important for you. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree. Because some things that I wanted to remember and that I wanted to take down, I didn't manage to put everything in the notebook. I have also said that I also had other notes that were hidden in another place, but I wasn't able to find them. I wanted to make it complete, to put everything in one notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Where were the other notes that you're now mentioning?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have them even today. They are put in a jar in a mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: When did you do at that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question, what "that" refers to. The diary or...

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No. When did you, as you say, put some other notes in a jar on a mountain?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the war. They were more safe in case I survived to find them. And this is what I did the documents of my family members when I joined the war. And I found everything after the war, the photographs and everything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So did the find the notes from the jar after the war?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to collect them. The time was not suitable for me to find them, the weather. And I didn't go there ever since. I know the place where it is and I'll sure that I'm going to find them there and that everything is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Have you ever mentioned this to anyone before?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. I don't think I have mentioned this, but this is true. I know that I have said for the diary that it isn't something important, that there were some loose papers, some notes and that that was not important, the thing that you're calling a diary. I wanted to make a diary out of it, but it isn't actually a diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So what important things are missed out of this diary that you're now explaining might be in notes in a jar?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Things that happened during the war. They are noted down and these are things about the war, things that happened during the war. Papers, documents; private, official.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now the specific point I want to ask you of course is the meeting on or about the 15th of May when Limaj said he was general commander of the zone. Did you note that down?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I believe, yes, I have made notes about this case. But not on the spot. This is simply something private. I wasn't there in the capacity of a journalist to interview someone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Please understand, no one is suggesting that you were there as a Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. journalist. We have seen the diary and I would like you, now have it in front of you, for you to turn to the page or pages which deal with the dates in May and in particular the page -- I can give you the number that has been stamped at the top of it which deals with the 12th of May. Now that is, on your copy, it's our page 8 your copy is 00036994.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, if you -- you've seen it before so I don't want to take a lot of time reading it out at this stage. But just glance down that page in your diary you see you deal with the 12th of May, ending with the words "Celiku 3 "which I will come back to in a minute. And then over the page there is an entry on the 14th written about something which had happened which you knew about. Do you see that on the next page, the 14th, yes?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And then on the next page after that there is the heading the 21st of May. Again, not as a journalist, just things that have happened to you during the war. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: The short point is that nowhere on these pages do you record an event as important as Fatmir Limaj coming to say he was the general commander and who else was in charge and the name of the unit, do you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did wrote the -- I did write the name of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... we'll come to that. But you don't record in this diary any meeting addressed by Fatmir Limaj in which he told you significantly that he was the commander and that the name of the unit was Celiku 3, do you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have noted things, not things that were not important to me. Many things are not even today interesting for me. As for my friends or things that I was interested in, I did take notes of those things. I -- I don't know what you meant. It is true that I have not write -- I did not write down anything about that meeting, but that meeting must be mentioned somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: My final question on that topic, the meeting with Fatmir Limaj, it isn't mentioned anywhere in the diary.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe it is like that. I didn't have this with me and I haven't read it. If it's not there, then that stands.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, would that be a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I know that I have noted down this meeting somewhere. It should be somewhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mansfield. We'll have the break now. Unfortunately the need to redact that name involves tracking over some 15 minutes of tape. So I'm told we will need the full half-hour break, to resume at ten minutes past. I'm sorry what that is doing to time, but that is the need technically. We will resume at ten minutes past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mansfield.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, witness, we were dealing with your diary as it's called and the fact that this occasion or meeting when you say Fatmir Limaj attended in Lapusnik to indicate that he was the zone commander isn't in your diary. However I now want to deal with what is in your diary. If you go to 36994, please, in your copy. That's the number at the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: We have had on page 8, Your Honour, of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: What you have noted under the 12th of May on that page was that -- it was a day without any significant fighting or -- you were preparing yourselves and so forth. "In the evening, Lladrovci and several of his friends came to us and told us that we had to merge with the Celiku staff." And then of course it's the last sentence I want to ask you about. Because when you were asked to read this yourself, I noted down and it's on the transcript what you actually said yourself was in this last sentence on this page. And please bear with me. This is how you put it: "I also signed and thus the Lapusnik post got the name Celiku 3." Now that is what it says, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And I suggest to you, if you look carefully on the original which you have in front of us -- we don't have the original; we have a photocopy of the original. The full stop, in other words the punctuation for the end of that sentence, does not come after the Albanian word, I think it's "emrin," but comes after Celiku 3, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think I explained this. This is not the original. This is not a direct note. I took several notes I had written on slips of paper and I put it here and I think I explained what the 3 stands for. That day it was not called Celiku 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I appreciate that you have tried to explain it. And what I'm suggesting to you is that Celiku 3 which was your original explanation was not added later. You wrote all this out from a note relating to the 12th of May as something which had happened on the 12th of May. Do you follow? That's why I have asked you carefully about it.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, I want to -- if you wouldn't mind, go back to -- keep the diary, please. Go back to the document I'm using as a framework, namely, the one in tab 11, paragraph 4 (a), page -- in your Albanian version. It's the second typed page. Now, you've dealt with the incident as it's described there around the 15th of May, but I want to deal with another aspect of it. It's indicated that "Limaj said he was the general commander of the zone." Now I want to put to you clearly, without you making any assumptions, guesses or speculation or anything, you're not in a position to say, are you, firstly there that was a zone, and, secondly, that Limaj was commander of that zone, May, June, July of 1998, are you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No I'm not. In some places there were soldiers. But it was not called a zone; it was called a territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And you're not in a position to say, because would it -- on this topic -- you don't know about the zones or they were properly called subzones, when they were created, their areas of responsibility who their commanders and deputy commanders were, are you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew who was in Kroimire. I knew because people went there to join. I didn't know that by name. I knew only the pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: What -- what zone was Kroimire in, subzone? What subzone, as it was then called, later became a zone. What subzone was Kroimire in?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kroimire was a village. But there were members even there, members of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. I'll ask the question again: Which subzone was Kroimire in.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The part that divides the asphalt road from Lapusnik to Carraleve is the western Drenica or the upper Drenica, Eperme, as we say. The other one is the lower Drenica. This is what is -- has always been called. This is how people divided it, that part in their own minds and that part, upper Drenica contains Kroimire also. This is what I have in mind, this part of upper Drenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, just working on that basis, who was the zone commander for upper Drenica?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Who was the commander for the other part, the lower Drenica?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't know it then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: What I want to suggest to you is: You knew absolutely nothing about the command structure of the KLA, whether it existed, how much of it existed, and who was in it, did you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew some names. But I didn't know what functions or what grades they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And when you told this Tribunal as you did a few days ago, that Fatmir Limaj was above, Shukri Buja was above Luani, that was complete nonsense, wasn't it? You didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say this with relation to the 5th of May. Shukri Buja came later. But after the 15th of May, it is absolutely true, that he was a commander above Shukri Buja, above Luan and above the others. I don't know who was above them -- above him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: What makes you believe that he was above Shukri Buja and Luani when Shukri Buja came on the scene?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I based this on what Luani said or someone else, because everyone went directly to Klecka, to Celiku.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: See, what I suggest you're doing is your making a gross assumption based on the fact that people would go to Klecka from time to time. You're assuming, aren't you? You don't know that he was above those two. Shukri Buja was a subzone commander. And there's no dispute, Fatmir Limaj was never a subzone commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to object, Your Honours. If there could be -- there's a lot of confusion here in the questions about the time period that's being talked about. At times it's 15th of May, and the proposition that has just been put to the witness about Shukri Buja being a subzone commander, I think the evidence suggests is much later. So I think there is -- I think it's extremely confusing and clarification about the time period that we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: When did Shukri Buja come on the scene, according to you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shukri Buja came on the scene around the 15th of May. He came to Lapusnik. On the next day he went to Klecke and after a time in June, he became -- he went to Kroimire. From Kroimire in June -- sometime in June he went it Blinaje. That is the truth. And with respect to how he -- what are you saying that I am fantasising, I am giving you just an example, not more. Early June, one person was disarmed. He was a soldier in Fustica. Another one in Blinaje, at a later time. The soldier who would say disarmed in Fustica had a problem with Shukri Buja. He reported to Celiku in Klecke. On the next day, Celiku went together with Shukri Buja and disarmed this person. If you want me to give his name, can I do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: When Shukri Buja came in June, at that point, using that date, to be precise, what position did Shukri Buja occupy in June?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a time he was in Kroimire with Luan and they couldn't find a common language regarding who would be the commander. This is what the soldiers and Luan said. After a time, he became commander in Blinaje. It was early, June, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... precise as I've been asked to be. Now are you saying in June, when he became -- or middle of June when he became commander over Luani, that he was below Fatmir Limaj?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And I suggest to you in relation to that, at that time it is complete nonsense, above him Shukri Buja, at that time was the general commander or the general headquarters, not Fatmir Limaj at all. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about what I know. And what the General Staff or the general headquarters did and who was a member of this headquarters, this I didn't know then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And which zone was Shukri Buja in, in middle of June onwards? Which zone was it, subzone?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In middle -- in the June, he was in Blinaje. In the middle of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: When he became a zone commander as you indicated, which zone was it? What was its name?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not the question of a zone. I wasn't talking about zones. I talked about territories. That territory, which fell under the command of Klecke, Celiku, that includes also Blinaje. Shukri Buja was in the territory of Blinaje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Have you -- have you heard the name Nerodime zone?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know it very well. I know where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Then you will know very well the area of responsibility and it's villages which came within it; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Approximately. Not very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And Klecka certainly didn't come within it, did it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I want to go back, if I may, to the document paragraph 4. A few more matter that's rise on that page. After paragraph (a) where you mention Fatmir - I've dealt with the one incident of which there is an issue - if you go to (c), 4 (c) on that page, you will see there you mention the Lapusnik detention camp and that you went there on several occasions. Do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. On which page, please, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: It should be on your page -- hasn't got numbers I'm afraid. It's the second page. It should be towards the bottom of the second page. Paragraph 4. We're now on subparagraph (c).

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. There is another document here. Maybe it's here. I don't see it here. I have something else here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I think you now have it and we've pointed out 4 (c).

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, this is another topic, the camp itself and your visits to it. You still have, I hope, the green diary in front of you, do you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Do you appreciate -- do you appreciate that the diary makes absolutely no mention of a prison in Lapusnik or a detention camp in Lapusnik, does it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have time to go over it. I don't know what time you are -- what page are you talking about. What do you mean by this diary?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I mean all pages in the diary, every single page. There is no mention anywhere in that diary. And I suggest you must know that by now. It's just not there. It's not mentioned at all.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it's not, it's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Well, just explain how it's not, it's not.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there is something about detentions, the arrests of some persons, but I'm not sure. I don't know whether there is something about the prison or not. Maybe it wasn't interesting at all, that topic at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... a prison and so it's -- it's clear that there is a mention of such a thing, but nothing to do with Lapusnik. So it's clear, it's on our page 16 in which you do mention and I'll just -- it's under 1998 heading I'll just read in English for speed. "In the afternoon Islam and I went to an oda, which was a sort of a military prison," and you saw somebody (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: But just coming back to Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I beat the living daylights out of two prisoners. With regard to mentioning that, I know that it's mentioned somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, as you raise that point, perhaps you'd like to you'd like to find it. That particular entry. In our version of the diary, it's on page 17 under the heading 1998. And I think on yours it's 3712, 37012, 37012.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Excuse me, if I might, I'm sorry to interrupt. I think we need a redaction at page 42 lines 18 to 20. I think -- it's not caught very well in the transcript, but part of is caught and I think from -- that it could identify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The reference to the name of a person may be the problem. Is that what you're pointing to?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It is. In fact, there were two persons mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. That will be redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, Witness, do you have your page in the diary, 37012, where there's 1998 written part way down the page and then it should read -- it's on our page 17: "This morning I met" -- I'm not going to read out any more names. You met somebody. At around 10. Have you got that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: A little lower down: "In the evening," and you mention a name. I won't read it out. "I went into the bunker in which there were two prisoners." Just to get it clear this is it not Lapusnik, is it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: "In which there were two prisoners. We beat the living daylights out of them." That's how it reads in our English version.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this page, 012, it's not written. In -- this figure, 1998 that you are mentioning in this part. Yes, yes, excuse me, I found it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: It says very clearly and these are words that I put to you yesterday and you denied them. This is where I got it from. "We beat the living daylights out of them." It suggests very clearly you did. Is it true?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says -- it's not -- he's trying to make a difference between the words, we beat the living daylight out of them. We didn't beat them strongly. Much. The point is we beat them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now I want to return to the particular topic I'm dealing with. Are you really saying to this Tribunal that the reason there is no mention of Lapusnik as a detention camp or a prison or your visits to it Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. is because it might not have been any interest to you. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the moment maybe it was not interesting to me. I didn't see doesn't interest -- interest me generally. But maybe that particular day it didn't were interest me, to write something about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, to make a rather long story short at no time in 1998 when you had occasion to sit down and write in this diary - or in 1999 because we know there are entries in 1999 - at no time occur to you that there was anything interesting to you or anybody else to make notes about this. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't think it was of any interest to me or to anyone. To me it was not of interest.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I have to put it to you that in fact the reason nothing is there is you yourself had nothing to do with, didn't see, unaware of, any prison camp. Otherwise it's the one thing you would have put down in there. Isn't it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not a complete diary. It just comprises some notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: If you would kindly go back to the document 4 -- paragraph 4. I'm dealing with (c) where you mention or where it is mentioned that you will testify in relation to the detention camp. A particular occasion is mentioned. I'm not going to read out the name. The first time you went there was a few prisoners. There's a name mentioned I won't read it out. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You have given evidence -- I'm not going to read out the transcript of what you have said about this person, but you've said a fair amount about him, that you saw him on the first occasion and you saw him much later before he met his death and at that time that he met his death. Do you remember saying all that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you this: In relation to that, do you realise that have you been shown photographs by the investigators of people said to be victims from the -- from the camp? Do you remember being shown photographs?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. But they didn't tell me that they were victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No, I'm sure they may not have. Do you appreciate that when you were shown a photograph of this individual, you did not recognise him. Did you realise that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that I saw this person in the photo. They didn't ask me whether I know this person as such. They simply showed me some photographs. The persons I knew I said I know. The ones I didn't know the names of and who they were, I didn't say I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And one of the people you said you didn't recognise was this individual.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible. I don't know. It is possible. I didn't say anywhere that this was this person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You've also told this Tribunal about another incident relating to - and I'm not going to name anybody again - two Serbs who were, you say, released. Do you remember talking about them?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And once again, I'm going to ask you to be careful about not making any assumptions, not speculating and so forth. And I'll take it shortly. Would it be right to say that whatever had happened to them and whenever they were released that you have no idea whether Celiku had anything to do with that at all, did you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I am certain that he didn't arrest them and that he -- that he hasn't given any orders for their arrest.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Or their release.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
