utterances.text: I heard -- with regard to the release, I heard that they were going to be released. At -- in an interview, at a later time, Celiku spoke that he released them. I didn't see when he took them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, I just want to ask but that. When do you say you saw an interview?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that same night.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On television. Either that night or the next day. It was broadcast on television. First it was in the radio. Then on television it was an interview relayed through -- the television of Albanian, the Albanian television.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, I just want to go back because of information that we've recently received to the question of the diary in relation to these matters and the notes which you say were in a jar. The diary you indicated earlier this afternoon had been provided to the investigators a day or so after the interview in May 2003. Now, I'd like you to think again; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not the way you're saying. It is either that you have received a wrong interpretation. I said what has been noted down has been noted down there. As for other notes, they are not put in this book because they are somewhere else. This is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. I'll take it in stages. When did you hand over the diary to the investigators?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the day that I mentioned. I believe it was the next day or on the same day. The next day is the maximum date. I don't know exactly when it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I appreciate that. It's a year or so ago. The first time you mentioned the diary -- I have already been over this, but because it's because of something had an I recently received. When I first asked you about this, I indicated that you had mentioned the diary on two times in the May 2003 interview. You then said in relation to this question that you had handed the diary over a day or so after that. Now is that what you think happened?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I mentioned it, they asked me, Do you have it? I said, I don't know, have I to look. Because of the things that you mentioned that were taken out. But what I know is that I handed it over immediately or shortly after. It's not that I took it from somewhere. This diary I had it with me all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Then if you had it with you all the time, why was it not received by the investigators until the 31st of October, 2003?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the exception of that day, when the things were taken out, I wasn't sure. And as for why they didn't get it, again, I don't know why. What I know is that I don't believe it was taken on the 31st of October. I believe that it was taken during the interviews. And this is what I think now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You see, in your statement, the most recent one, the one compiled over many days, December 2003 into January 2004, you indicate that it was in fact in October 2003 that you handed it over. Now, there weren't any interviews going on at that time. The interviews had happened in May and then in June and then you make a statement. The only other thing had been your appearance in front of the judge. See, what I'm trying to get at is where this diary had been kept and the -- as you say now for the first time, the existence of other notes. So I want you to think very carefully back to May. When you tell the investigators straightaway that have you got a diary, do you say that you handed it over then?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he said that, I'm not saying that I said that in May or in June. But when I mentioned this, I handed over this diary immediately on that day or the next day it was very hot. I was working in the garden. And this is a day when I hand overed this diary. I don't think it handed it over in October. Because I don't believe I had an interview in October of that year.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm having to ask you carefully because I dare say we will be told there are no notes of the handover of the diary. So when you were in the garden, as you now seem to recall you were, did an investigator come to the garden to get it or did you go to an office and hand is over?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He didn't come to the garden. But he passed by a nearby road and that's where I handed it over to him. And some pictures as well, sorry. There was some pictures inside the diary. Some personal, my pictures.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. By "pictures," do you mean photographs?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the same time with the diary I handed over some photographs as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, I don't wish you to, obviously, reveal anything personal. The question I have is: Do the photographs relate to anything that had happened in the war which you have described to this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't describe this or say this to the Tribunal. But I said that these were personal photographs that relate to the war and to the period after the war. These are some photographs from the beginning until the end of the war. Later on I didn't mention these photographs and I don't think that someone asked me about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No. Once again, rather like the notes in the jar, this is the first time that we've heard about them. Perhaps you can help us: How many photographs were there?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, what is in the jar is something else. What I'm saying now about the photographs, these are personal photographs from the war. And they were inside the diary on the day when I handed it over. As for it's jar, that contains other documents, other notes. It is not here. It is in a place where I have placed it during the war and this is what I said before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes I will concentrate on the photographs, if you wouldn't mind. How many photographs were there roughly?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About seven or eight photographs. It is possible that there was seven or eight photographs that were taken during the war in Lapusnik and other places. There could be a photograph from another place as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Do I understand that you took the photographs with your own camera?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was a person who was taking photographs there. He was a -- sort of a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. And does this soldier give you copies of the photographs?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These photographs were made by the person who was there and he gave me the copies during the war. He gave copies to everyone who was in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we go into private session so I can get an identity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Just so it's clear, you have indicated the identity of a soldier who took photographs. I ask you again: Did you take photographs?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I went and made a photograph in Malisevo with another person. We were two persons. I didn't have a camera. I had a camera later on, in 1999, but not at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: The reason I ask you is that, were any of the photographs that were handed over in the diary, photographs taken by you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't take photographs. There was other person who was taking photographs. But I was in the photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: The reason I ask you is that your diary - it's our page 19 - you can look it up if you wish. But your diary suggests that you did I'm going to read you a sentence without the names in the English version, page 19. "I took some photographs then as I did during that day with" -- and then you give a name. Why have you written in your diary "I took some photographs then." The date is the 13th of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which page it is. Can you help me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I have looked quickly. I think the 13th of March appears on your page 37017. That's where it starts.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And then if you look on the next page, 37018, towards the bottom of the page, the name I haven't read out is there and just before it - I obviously don't attempt the Albanian - just before the name the two lines from the bottom. "The sentence we have is I took some photographs then, as I did during that day with..." And then you mention somebody.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is true. And I said before that in 1999 I had my camera. It is possible that I one in the end of 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, the next question is: Do you know where these photographs that you handed over in the diary, do you know where they are now?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe they were returned to me. The photographs were returned to me, and I believe that all the ones that I handed over were there, when they were returned. When I handed them over, I didn't count them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: When were they returned to you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Last year.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Where are they now?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They're with me. Maybe they have copies. I haven't asked them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: When you say "they're with me," do you mean they're with you now?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... are they in -- I'm not asking for the place. Are they in another place?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are not here. They are in my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Were you ever asked any questions about the photographs by the investigators?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They asked me who is in the photograph, where were these photographs taken. To my recollection, there are dates on these photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm sorry to ask you for your help in this -- some time ago, but we know nothing of this. When did that occur that somebody sat done with you or stood up, whatever they did, to get the details of that photograph? When did that happen?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe when I came here, it was then. This is what I know, and I'm telling you what I know and what I'm sure of. This is what I have given, and I can be held responsible for that, that I gave these photographs and that they were returned to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, the position you say, when you came here, do you mean when you came here to make the statement or when you came here to give evidence?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, you're right. When I was transferred from Kosova I came straight to an interview in Holland, after five or six days.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Were the questions and the answers about the photographs noted down?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And I want to ask you this: Why didn't you tell whoever it was -- do you happen to know who the person was who was taking down your answers about the photographs? Who was it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the person whom I handed over the diary and the photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. Who is that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is an OTP worker, and I know that his last name is Lehtinen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Why didn't you tell him, since you were dealing with the diary and also the photographs, well, certainly the photographs, why didn't you tell him, Oh, by the way, there are some other notes hidden away in a jar?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I thought that I might not find them. I don't know. As I said, I didn't think this would be important. Even now I think that this diary is not important for someone else or for the Court. This is something personal. They mentioned it, they asked for it, and I handed it over to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm going to pass from that topic it a final topic, if I may, with you. And the final topic is the burial of Alushani. And I want to suggest like much of what you have told the Tribunal about Lapusnik and so forth, you haven't even told the truth about the recovery of his body, have you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I told the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, looking at what you have so far said about this, that his body was recovered after three days. That isn't true, is it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: His body was recovered after it had stayed there for two full days. It was recovered on the third day. This is what I know. And the body missed one of the arms. It didn't have one of the arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And the reason I suggest you are unable to say how long it remained, I'm going to suggest it only was left for 24 hours before it was in fact recovered on the 27th. The reason, I suggest, that you are wrong about all this, is that you had nothing to do with it, did you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I didn't go to take the body because I was injured. That was impossible for me. The people gathered themselves, including his brother. They formed groups and they went. I didn't go down the Berisa Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: The reason I'm asking these questions is because --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So again it's clear where I'm getting it from, it's Day 54.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: The answer that has been transcribed about there when you were asked the question what happened with his body, the answer is: "I'm not certain about the date, but after three days we dragged his body from Lapusnik." Now that's what's been -- there is a bit more to it than that. "And what happened after that. We buried him in Klecka."

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear the whole translation it Albanian. But it is true that I said we recovered his body after three days. Three days after he was killed. The body remained there for two full days and was recovered on the third day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: But not by you.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't go down there. I stayed on the top of the hill, of the Berisa hill. And I organised the ones who would go, those that could go. Because it was dangerous to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, since you say that, who did you organise? And we'd like the names, please, of those people you say you organised to deal with this. Because I suggest that you are making it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know whether it's necessary I have a list of names and it may be sensible not to read them in public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: We have dealt with names of people who might be connected with the removal of Alushani's body in private session. I don't intend to repeat the names. But I think what you do accept now is that you personally had nothing to do with actually removing his body. You did not actually participate in that, did you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mansfield. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: My name is Gregor Guy-Smith and I represent Haradin Bala. I'd like to start off asking you what I belief should be some relatively simple questions, if I could. Which are: Your memory concerning when you spoke with members of the OTP off the record. The first time that you spoke with members of the OTP off the record was sometime before your interview on May 27th, 2003; correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you have a conversation with members of the OTP before that time?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. On the day we had the conversation, that's the day when it was recorded. Not before that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, before you had a recorded conversation with members of the OTP there was a discussion with them about whether or not you were being considered as a suspect or as a witness; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The content of the summons was clarified and this was the discussion before.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Precisely. And the content of the summons which was clarified which was, as you put it, was the discussion before was a discussion that was not recorded by anyone, to your knowledge, was it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I don't know that they took notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Where was this discussion held?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day, before the recording started. Sometime before the recording started.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, you've told me when. But my question was: Where. Where was that discussion held?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was held in the same office where the recording took place. And if you want to know the place, I can tell you. It was Lipjan.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the time that that discussion was being had, who was present?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two persons and an interpreter. Three persons in all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you identify who those people are, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As for their first names I know that one of them was called Alex. The other was Lehtinen. And the interpreter -- if I think here, if I have some time, maybe his name will come to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Was the interpreter who you were talking with Alex and Lehtinen with the same interpreter that you spent the day with on May 27th during your recorded interview?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I were to give you the name of Duram Bani [phoen] would that refresh your recollection concerning who that person was?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: After you had the conversation that was recorded on May 27th, did you have a telephone call or conversation with Mr. Lehtinen?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a talk with him about the submission of the diary. That was later. And they called for me in my family because I did not appear on the date when I was supposed to appear.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say you had a conversation concerning it's diary that was later that conversation was a conversation you had on May 27th, is that your testimony? So that we're clear.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know. As for 27th of May I don't know. On the 27th, I said that I will come. They called on the phone, on my son's phone, and I told them that I was going to go, and I asked them where this would take place. This was the whole conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Now after you finished your recorded interview on May 27th with Alex and Mr. Lehtinen, did you have a conversation that night with Mr. Lehtinen on the telephone concerning your recorded interview?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't remember talking about the interview, and I don't remember this conversation, if I had one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Before you met with members of the OTP on June 17th, did you any other contact with any members of the OTP? So that would be between the dates of May 28th and June 16th.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a contact, but I don't remember when it occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Was that a personal contact, did you meet someone in person, or was that over the telephone?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was a direct conversation, a personal contact. We went to Lapusnik, but I don't remember when -- the time when this happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you recall who was present at the time that you had a direct contact?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two persons. One was driving. I don't remember his name for the moment. The other was Mr. Lehtinen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: How long a period of time were you with the individual who was driving and Mr. Lehtinen when you went to Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to get to Lapusnik and come back, it takes you at least one hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is that one hour each way, or is that a total travel time of an hour that you're speaking about?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. To go and come back. It takes you an hour for both ways.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the period of time that you were travelling to Lapusnik, while you were at Lapusnik and on your way back were Lapusnik, during that period of time, were you appear of whether or not the conversation you were having with Mr. Lehtinen was recorded?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think there was a conversation with the exception of the fact that we went there to see Lapusnik. I don't think that it was recorded. Maybe there is an equipment that can record that, but I don't think it was recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the period of time that you were in the car, on the way there, was Mr. Lehtinen, to your knowledge, taking any notes?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know. They had a camera for taking photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you arrived at Lapusnik, I take it that you stayed at Lapusnik for some period of time, did you not?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. For some 15 to 30 minutes approximately. This is what I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During that 15 to 30 minute period that you believe that you were at Lapusnik, were photographs being taken?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think yes, photographs I think photographs were taken, three or four.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And during that period of time while those photographs were being taken did you have a conversation with Mr. Lehtinen in which you were describing your time at Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. This is something known, this was something that was known, something that I said before to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What you said to them before would have been contained in your interview of May 27th; correct? That is the extent of which you had said to them before; right?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here I'm talking about the period after 27th of May, because your question was for the period between the 27th of May and 16th of July.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: June, correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And as you have testified the only time you had any contact with him in terms of a recorded interview was the recorded interview that you have spent some time having a conversation with Mr. Mansfield about, and that was on the 27th of May; right?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who Mr. Mansfield is. And if I had nothing to do with him. Or it was the translation. Please, repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I can assure you have had something to do with Mr. Mansfield. You and he have been talking with each other for over a day. He is the gentleman to my left, who just finished asking questions.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know, but I thought that you referred to a person from before who has the same name. Because it can happen that there are few persons with the same name. And what was translated to me in Albanian was not clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Are you having difficulty with the translation that is occurring as questions are being asked of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, absolutely not. I just said that only that sentence was mixed up for a moment. It wasn't complete. I just heard the name Mansfield.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you were at Lapusnik, did you direct Mr. Lehtinen to take photographs of places that you believed were important?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't take him. We went to the place where I had been to, and up to the place where Ymer was killed. Up to the monument. He took a picture of the monument. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And apart from taking photographs, did you have a conversation with Mr. Lehtinen while you were at Lapusnik concerning, for example, the placement of any buildings?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the places, yes. Where they were positioned. But as for buildings, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the places, as you put it, where they were positioned, did you have a map that you were working with?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As I said, we went through the road that goes from position number 2 up to the place where the monument is. Only on that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you have any paper with you, on which you jotted down any notes to show Mr. Lehtinen where you believe positions were?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know those positions very well am and I know all of the houses there. But I didn't have any paper with me and any notes with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you returned from Lapusnik, did you go back and continue a recorded interview on that day?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As I said, this did not occur on the day of the interview. This happened on another day. I don't remember when it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And that's a memory that you have quite clear in your mind, I take it? As regarding your Lapusnik interview with Mr. Lehtinen. Correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said there wasn't an interview in Lapusnik. No interview took place there Lapusnik, and I don't even think there was an interpreter. I don't remember seeing an interpreter. And if there wasn't an interpreter there, my English at that time was limited.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, then -- to use your -- your words, since you said there wasn't an interview, I will call it your visit to Lapusnik. When you went to Lapusnik on a visit with Mr. Lehtinen, do you remember what time of the day this occurred?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This occurred in the afternoon, but I don't know the date or the day. It was an afternoon, around 4.00, 5.00, in the afternoon. 3.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you went on your visit to Lapusnik, could you tell us, if you remember now, the next time that you were involved in a recorded interview?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when the second time occurred. I had two interviews, one in May and one later.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if I were to tell that you your second interview was in June it lasted for two days would that refresh your memory as to when you had your interview in June?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, there two interviews one in May and the other I don't when. It was in June. I don't know the date. I don't remember the date. And this is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the interview in June, do you recall how long it was?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As you sit here today, do you recall if it lasted for one or two days? Did you have interviews only for one day, or did you have interviews for a series of days; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One day, 12 hours. There was an interview that would take even longer. From 10.00 in the morning until 4.00 in the afternoon. With interruptions, with breaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would hope. It's a long time to have an interview. After your interview in June, did you have any further contact Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. with any member of the OTP in the month of July?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A contact, yes, but not an interview. I mentioned that I had a contact a day before. On the day that I was arrested or I don't know exactly what day it was, when I went on an interview with the police, I met Mr. Lehtinen for a couple of minutes. This was a time that the German policeman allowed him to have with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What did you discuss with Mr. Lehtinen at that time when the German policeman allowed you to have a conversation with him?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was there, present, the policeman. He allowed us to speak for a couple of minutes. He asked me about the arrest, what happened, these things. Nothing more.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you tell him about the arrest and what had happened?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He knew about this. I did not invite him. He came there on his own will.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: This is not my question. You said, "He asked me about the arrest, what happened, these things. Nothing more." And my question to you was: "Did you tell him about the arrest and what happened." Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In two, three words I told him that I arrested, that some things were seized.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: After that conversation with Mr. Lehtinen in July did you have any further contact with him or any other member of the OTP during the month of July?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In August?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think in September, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In September when you had contact with some member of the OTP, where were you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did some member of the OTP come to visit you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two persons. One of them was Mr. Lehtinen, a female interpreter, and I don't remember the other person. Maybe there were three. Two or three. I believe there were two.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: How long a period of time did they spend with you, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a time around dinner. It began before the dinner. Maybe as much as they were given time, approximately 30 minutes or 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And what was the subject matter of your conversation. What were you talking about with them in September, while you were in prison, when they came to visit?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About the prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is that the extent of your conversation? Just about the prison?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe they didn't ask anything else about the interview. They just asked about the prison. They asked me who my lawyer was, what I was thinking, what was going to happen, and stuff like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you have any further contact, apart from your one prison visit in September, with any member of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I appeared in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you appeared in court, did you have some contact with a member of the OTP before your court appearance, where they discussed matters with you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No matter was discussed. There was no interpreter. I just saw that one of them was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll resume at five minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In the month of October, you had a series of meetings with the OTP, did you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't have many meetings. Didn't have meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you have any meetings with the OTP in October of 2003?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I met them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember very well. But I think I already stated here what happened. I don't remember anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say that you don't remember anything else, is that with regard to the month of October that you are referring [sic], that you don't remember anything else or that you met with the OTP?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I meant October.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And so we're all clear, what you remember is meeting with them but you don't remember where; you don't remember when, other than it was the month of October; and you have no recollection whatsoever concerning the subject matter of that meeting. Is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think it was about some documents, about a document. But I'm not sure whether it was October or November. It was about a personal document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Can you give us any another information concerning this personal document, or is this something that we need to discuss in private?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't need -- I don't think we can discuss it in private session. I was taking care of a -- I was asking to have a passport issued to me with respect to the travel. I don't remember how often -- how many contacts I had, one, two, or three.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the period of time that you had a contacts, whether it be one, two are or three, did you have any discussion whatsoever concerning your time at Lapusnik in October? And by that I mean during the month of October, when you were having these meetings.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. We didn't discuss that. And there were other persons. I don't know if they were from the OTP. Maybe they were, but from what I remembered, they introduced themselves as being -- as working in another division. And that they were -- it was a discussion about these documents that I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We've almost finished with the year of 2003, and so I want to direct your attention to the month of November. In November, apart from the potential discussions you had concerning travel documents, did you have any contact with any members of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During these two or three times, I meant also the month of October. But we didn't discuss anything about the interview. It was about these travel documents that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And in December? I'm asking you the same question concerning December.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. In December, or in January, yes. Two or three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And each time that you met with the OTP during that period of time the discussion had something to do with travel documents and had nothing to do with the case in which you are presently testifying; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are asking me now about December. I answered about December and January. We had discussed then also about the statement or the interview. Something about the diary, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say that you had some discussion about the diary in December, do you recall when that was?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Who did you have the discussion with?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In December and in January I know that after I left Kosova I had one or two contacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you one or two contacts in December and January after you left Kosovo, who did you have them with?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the Prosecutor's office. If you want me to give names, I think they were the two persons I mentioned earlier. Mr. Lehtinen and Alex.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You told us that you had some discussion about the diary. And when you said you had some discussion about the diary, what was that discussion that you about the diary sometime in December or January?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We discussed when I took down the notes, at what time, in what place. Things like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, when you say that you had a discussion about when you took down the notes, at what time, and in what place, did you tell them when you wrote specific notes and where you were when you wrote them?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have told them what I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I appreciate that you may well have done that, but my question is a little bit different. Because you've indicated in your answer that you discussed when you took down the notes, at what time, and in what place. So once again my question do you is: Did you tell them what places you took these notes down in? I'll start with the place. Did you tell them you took the notes down in specific places?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What specific places did you tell them that you took the notes down in?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told them that I -- some of the notes I noted when I was in Pristina, some during the war. Such things.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, some during the war is a time, sir. It's not a place. And since you told us you were in a number of different places, where during the war did you tell members of the OTP that you took these notes?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told them that I took some of the notes in Lapusnik, in the way I told them about the way I took these notes. How I copied them later. Like when I was also in Nekovce.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We will return to the diary. I now want to go back, since we've finished the year of 2003, to your interview of May 27th, 2003, which I believe is the very first time that you had a recorded interview with members of the OTP; correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the first interview that was recorded. That was the first interview --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, during that interview, you discussed a gentleman by the name of Shala; correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And in that interview you discussed an incident that had occurred with Shala's son coming to Lapusnik; right?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I discussed about this that day. But I know that I have discussed this at a certain time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to see if this helps refresh your recollection with regard to what you discussed that day. And that's on page 16, the bottom of the page. You stated, in some -- concerning some questions about Shala: "And in the beginning when the war started, he was already a UCK soldier. He asked, he came to and begged me to admit his son into the UCK ranks and kept asking us for ten days because I wouldn't. I wouldn't accept this. I didn't admit his son because I thought I considered him as a problematic person at that time." And Mr. Whiting asks you: "The son?" And you respond: "Shala's son." Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say you don't remember that clearly, I take it you mean you don't remember having that discussion with Mr. Whiting on the 27th of May, about Shala's son; right?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what I wanted to say. I'm not sure it was during that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you recall talking to Mr. Whiting about Shala's son being a problem?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have never said that -- I don't remember to have said that he was a problematic person, that he was a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You have just said two things: You said you never said that and you don't remember saying it. And I want to make sure that we're clear about which it is. Are you telling us now that you never said that Shala's son was problematic?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I might have said that it was -- it might be a problem for time carry the pistol he had at that time. But I don't think I have said he was a problematic person because I didn't know him from before.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: With regard to Shala begging you to admit his son into the UCK, do you remember that occurring? And by "that," I mean do you remember Shala coming to you or having a conversation with you in which he begged you to admit his son into the UCK?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you remember telling Mr. Whiting that this occurred?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have told him what happened. This is what I believe I told him, but not what you are putting to me now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Younis, your help here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You're looking for the statement in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes, we have it here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: While that is occurring, I can continue for a moment. Thank you very much, Mr. Younis.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I would just note that I believe that the English -- no, it's the 17th of May 2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: 27th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: 27th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Just a note: I believe that the English is a transcript of the English that was spoken at the interview. In other words, it's an actual transcript of the English. The Albanian is an transcript of the actual Albanian spoken at the interview. So if I'm right about that --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: One would think then, and I'm asking for clarification now, that the document that I'm reading from is an accurate document with regard to the Albanian that was spoken. That is my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the answer is no. If -- the English is the -- I believe, looking at this transcript, that the English is a transcript of the English that was spoken at the interview. We have also provided the Albanian that was spoken at the interview. There may be differences between the two because of the natural problems that occur with on-the-spot translation. Just to clarify that, so that the Albanian may be slightly different in places from the English transcript. There is not, I believe, a translation of the Albanian transcript. If that is clear. I'm not sure that it's clear because I see quizzical looks.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think I understand that the document that I am relying upon may or may not be accurate with regard to what this gentleman said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No. I think that the point is it's important to put the Albanian in front of the witness because the witness may be able -- first of all, I think it's important if going to ask questions about the statement to put the statement to the witness. Secondly, the Albanian may contain some slight differences in wording from the English that you have and may be points to clarify in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Precisely. I said I may or may not have an accurate translation and I do not have a copy of this statement in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I thank counsel for conducting that notionally through the Bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sir, I would like you to take a look at what I believe purports to be an Albanian statement. And by that I mean the document is in the Albanian language, and it concerns the interview that you had on the 27th of May, 2003 with Mr. Whiting, Mr. Lehtinen and the services of an interpreter. Just looking at the very first page of that document, do you recognise, just reading to yourself --

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is the first time for me to see it today. But it looks like my answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say it's the first time for you to see it today, are you telling us that you have never seen that document before today?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. Not in writing. No, I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, it's going to take a minute to get to the place that I need to get to in this document, but I'll come to you with this momentarily. Did you have a conversation with Mr. Whiting concerning Shala's son at any time?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the conversation you had concerning Shala's son, did you tell Mr. Whiting that Shala's son wanted to join the KLA?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you tell Mr. Whiting that Shala asked you to help him in that regard, meaning to have his son join the KLA?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. I don't think I have mentioned that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you recall at any point in time, either in your May interview or in your June interview, discussing the question of Shala's son joining the KLA and you having a conversation with Haradin Bala who you have identified as one of the Shalas at Lapusnik concerning this matter?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think -- I don't remember, but I know about this case, and probably I have mentioned that. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now before the war, did you know Haradin Bala?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Before the war, did you know Haradin Bala's family?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said I have seen his father sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Had you seen Haradin Bala before the war?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Maybe I have seen him, but I don't remember to have talked with him or to have met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you know anything at all about Haradin Bala's father? Once again, before the war.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Haradin Bala's father was a famous singer, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. He sang folk songs.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: He travelled throughout Kosova singing folk songs at weddings an important events; correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And his name was what?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seliman Haradini.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you know him? Did you know Seliman Haradini?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen him several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you consider him a friend of yours?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say you had seen him several times had you seen him perform or had you actually sat down and had a cup of tea with the man?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen him while he was performing, but I remember when he was hospitalised together with one of my uncles, in the same room.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you ever have a meeting with Haradin Bala's son in which he asked to join the KLA?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He came to join the KLA, together with a cousin of his.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What was -- how old did you have to be to join the KLA?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Normally you have to be 18. But there have been some who were younger than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: How old was Shala's son?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe 16, 17. He was young.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say he was young, you believe he was 16, 17 years old at that time that he came to join the KLA; right?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I want to say he was around about 18 years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... how old?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 18. Less, maybe. He looked young. 17, 16, 18. He was a well-built boy.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that Haradin Bala's son was born in 1986, on June 10th?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... if I'm not mistaken about 12 years old in the summer of 1998, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This I don't know. He said that he is a son of Haradin, that his father was there. He was carrying a pistol, 765, and I took away that pistol from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I want you to take a look now at the transcript in front of you that purports to be in Albanian and take a look at page 14, down at the bottom of the page. And if you could read that to yourself. Did you give --

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And did you give Mr. Whiting this particular answer concerning this issue concerning Haradin Bala's son wishing to join the KLA: "And in the beginning when the war started, when he was already UCK soldier he asked -- he came to and begged me to admit his son into the UCK ranks and kept asking me this for ten days because I wouldn't accept this. I didn't admit his son because I considered him as a problematic person at that time." Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not on page 14 on the bottom as you said in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Going to page 15. Reading through that page. I believe it starts off [Albanian spoken], right? My pronunciation I'm sure is abysmal. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now when speaking to Mr. Whiting you told Mr. Whiting that Mr. Bala was begging to you have his 12-year-old son become a member of the KLA; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Objection. That is not what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I have taken some licence. I do apologise. I'll rephrase.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You told Mr. Whiting that Haradin Bala begged you to have his son join the KLA; correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I have said this, but even if I have, then I have made a mistake. I don't think I have said this or that he has asked me -- he has begged me to take his son. Because he could have well done that himself. He might have asked the commander to admit his son. If I said this, I have made a mistake. This was not as it was then.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, when you gave this statement on May 27th after you had been told that you were no longer a suspect but a witness, at that time when you were being asked questions, you were, I assume attempting to be accurate and help Mr. Whiting in his pursuits. Correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less. Because I didn't want to think about the war at that time anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now in this same answer, you also say that you used to go to the Drenica region and in the beginning when the war started, when he was already an UCK soldier. I take it there you were referring to Shala. Correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't understand what I meant. I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say that you don't understand what you meant, what you're telling us now is that you sit here reading this today this particular passage I take it makes no particular sense to you. It must have been a mistake or a fantasy.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know first where it is written and I don't know whom I meant when I mentioned that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this then: After you answer a question concerning Shala's son as it is written in the transcript, Mr. Whiting asks you a question which is, I believe: "Okay. Was this at Lapusnik that this happened?" Which I believe is the top -- now we're on page 15. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Is it in the beginning of the page?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure, but I would suggest to you -- you know what I'm going to do? Hold on for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It is one, two, three, four, five, six, seven lines down from the top of the page, sir. Starting with the word "kur."

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I can read it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good. Now Mr. Whiting asks you: "Was this at Lapusnik that this happened?" And you respond, "Yes." And then Mr. Whiting asks you: "Okay. If you came to Lapusnik around the 9th of May, did Shala come around same time? You respond: "Later." He says: "He came later?" You respond: "Yes." And Mr. Whiting asks you: "How much later, do you remember?" And you say: "Well, probably a week after or two weeks after." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see it, when it's written about ten days.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now that would mean that according to your recollection Shala arrived Lapusnik around the 19th of May; correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe even later.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, when you say "maybe even later," right here what you have told us is approximately two weeks. Right?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, yes. I don't know the date when he came.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: But in May of 2003 when you were giving this particular interview, when you were asked this particular question concerning when you believe Shala to arrived at Lapusnik, you said: "It was a week after or two weeks after." That's what you told Mr. Whiting, because that is what you remembered then. Right?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. If it is written down, then this is what I said. This is what I remembered.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As you sit here today, are you now changing that memory to maybe being even later?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the date when Haradin Bala came to Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is the answer that you have given here similar to the answer that you gave with regard to Haradin Bala's son, which is that it's just something that you don't know? Something that you have made a mistake about?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to object. I would just note actually what he says is probably a week or two weeks after. Not -- not a week or two weeks after. He does qualify it in the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the difficulty I think you can appreciate is "probably" a term of art which is sometimes used for various purposes and I'm not going to go any further than that at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Difference with a week or two weeks with or without a probably and ten days can be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As you sit here today, can you tell us as you remember when the gentleman, Haradin Bala, who you also call Shala, came to Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know that he came later, or that I saw him later. I didn't see him during the first ten days. Maybe not even during the first 15 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, my understanding is that you didn't know Haradin Bala before the war but you became good friends during the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had conversations together. I didn't know him from before the war. Maybe I knew him before the war, but I don't remember having conversation with him. From his appearance, I could think that I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well is this a matter of speculation or reverie with regard to whether you think you could have known him? Is that a man that you talked to during the war at Lapusnik, is that what you're telling us? Or is that something that you think might have happened?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war you can say that it is a speculation. It is not clear to me and I have never said that I have known him and that I have spent time with him, talked to him. But during the war I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What about after the war? After the war -- did you become good friends after the war?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were friends. I didn't say good friends. We were comrades in arms. We didn't have anything bad going on between us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, after the war when you were friends, as you put it comrades in arms, you met him lots of times, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that during the war we were friends and that continued. After the war I met him once or twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No. My question is not once or twice, sir. My question is: Didn't you have a relationship with Haradin Bala after the war where you met him lots of times and you have become his good friend? Isn't that what happened?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said that I met him during the memorial and I also met him when he came to fix his vehicle together with a relative of his, a close relative, maybe his son.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So the thing that I have just said is something that you would have never said, that after the war you met Haradin Bala a lot of the times and you have become good friends. That is something that you wouldn't have said, correct, because that wouldn't be true?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never said that we were good friends. We were friends. I don't remember saying this. And if I have said that, then it wasn't with a particular intention. I didn't specify good friends or bad friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, what happens this is an appropriate moment to digress for but a second. You told us just the other day that you believed that you had a good memory. However, heroin did destroy white cells in your brain, if I'm not mistaken. Do you, as you sit here right now, have memory difficulties?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I have difficulties. And what you just said is wrong. Either you're saying it wrong or you got it wrong. What I said yesterday was that those who use heroin, the heroin destroys the white cells in their brains and that they can forget. But I don't have problems with my memory. Maybe I cannot see that myself, but I personally think that I don't have problems with my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: But for a brief moment, are you still using any, as you call it, therapy to deal with your heroin past?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not even an aspirin or paracetamol, never. I don't like medicaments.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When was the last time that you self-administered your therapy, as you called it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was in prison. And after that I didn't get any therapy.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the particular medication that you say you were using was what precisely?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, then. When you were in prison and you were self-medicating.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had some tablets with me for two or three days. And after those days, I didn't have any.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And what -- once again, what particular medication was that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, but it was part of the therapy that I was receiving. Something that was in my pocket.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: This therapy that you were receiving, had you received a prescription for this therapy? And by that I mean had the doctor that you told us about written out for you a course of medical treatment so that you could assist yourself?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was prescribed, this therapy, and the time when and how to use it was designated.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Returning to Mr. Bala, you said you met Mr. Bala a couple of times after the war. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, during the war when you spoke to Mr. Bala, can you tell us about how many times you had conversations with him?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several times even then. We were in different places. We didn't meet often.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, "several" is an elusive concept here so I'm going to need a little help when you use at that word "several." That doesn't work particularly well in terms of telling us how many times you met and talked with him. So could you give us a number?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seven or eight times. Surely I met him for seven or eight times not to say there were more, but I think that I did meet him several -- seven or eight times.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And during this seven or eight times that you claim to met him, would it be fair to say that you talked about things such as family?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably, yes. You don't mention families during the war a lot, but it could be that families were mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As you sit here today, you have no recollection of discussing anything about his family with him; correct? This friend of yours.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said was, yes, we did discuss that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: How many children does he have?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. He has several children. And the meetings that I mentioned occurred during the war and some of them after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, after the war, when you talked to him about stuff after the war, did you find out how many sons he has, how many daughters?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. We spoke of something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: After the war, did you found out what his wife's name was?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. I don't know even where his house is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What about his health? What do you know about his health?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that when I met him on the occasion when he was fixing his car, he said that his health was not very good. And then during -- when we went to visit, to pay condolences to someone -- to the family of someone who had died, he mentioned that he had heart problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was after the war. Probably a year or two after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Where was this conversation, a year or two after the war?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I met him for the last time, it was when he was fixing his car. And it was just before he was arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What did he tell about his health condition when he was -- when you met him that last time when he was fixing his car? What did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. He said that something was wrong, but we spoke of something else. We didn't speak of health very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So as you sit here today, would it be fair to say that you don't remember any conversation about his health, and you've never had a conversation with him about any aspect of his family that you can remember; correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I know that we spoke about health, and I know what else we spoke of on that day. We spoke of cars and something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It is but a few minutes to 7.00. I'm about to go into a long area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Guy-Smith. That obviously is a convenient time. As indicated, we will now need to adjourn until Wednesday afternoon next. Sir, I'm afraid with the break in sittings here, it will be necessary for your evidence to continue next week on Wednesday afternoon. And those assisting you will give you details of when you should be here and what should happen in the interval. We will now adjourn, to resume on Wednesday at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
